title: The Great Banquet
reflectionText: The people first invited all had good reasons to stay away — a field, some oxen, a new marriage. So the table was filled instead with the poor, the crippled, the blind, and the lame, brought in from the streets and the roads. The feast went on without the ones who were sure they had time; the passage does not pretend they lost nothing. What ordinary, reasonable thing keeps you saying "later" to the table?
editorialNotes: PAL Daily supervised production, Batch H completion pass. Luke 14:15-24 ONLY. Owner-approved shortScripture:true — naturally 236w WEB / 214w KJV from a 232-word passage; not padded. Retains the invitation and 'everything is ready' (14:17), the three excuses (field, oxen, marriage, 14:18-20), the master's anger as stated (14:21), the invitation to the poor/maimed/blind/lame (14:21), the second sending into roads and hedges with 'compel them to come in' (14:23), and the closing exclusion of the originally invited (14:24). No extra invitees or excuses invented; the anger is not softened; 'compel' is rendered as the text gives it, not as physical force or coercive conversion; the exclusion is not erased. WEB v24 keeps 'many are called, but few are chosen'; KJV v24 ends at 'taste of my supper' (per each lane's text). primaryCharacterId 'jesus'.
